requirements.claim:
BLIP-2 pre-trains its Q-Former in two stages: a first vision-language representation learning stage with a frozen image encoder, and a second vision-to-language generative learning stage with a frozen LLM.
In the representation learning stage, three pre-training objectives inspired by BLIP are jointly optimized with shared input format and model parameters, each using a different attention masking strategy between queries and text to control their interaction.
The representation learning stage trains the Q-Former so its queries learn to extract visual representation most informative of the text, while the generative stage connects the Q-Former to a frozen LLM and uses projected query embeddings as soft visual prompts to condition the LLM on the Q-Former's visual representation.
The first (representation learning) stage jointly optimizes three pre-training objectives inspired by BLIP, sharing the same input format and model parameters, with each objective using a different query-text attention masking strategy.
The first stage aims to train the Q-Former such that its queries learn to extract visual representation that is most informative of the text, using image-text pairs with a frozen image encoder.
The second (generative pre-training) stage connects the Q-Former with frozen image encoder to a frozen LLM, projecting query embeddings via a fully-connected layer to the LLM text embedding dimension and prepending them as soft visual prompts.
The second stage harvests the frozen LLM's generative language capability, with the Q-Former acting as an information bottleneck that feeds useful visual information and mitigates catastrophic forgetting.

(2021) on image-text pairs, with contrastive similarities computed as the dot product of mean-pooled image encoder outputs and mean-pooled BERT outputs. Stage 1 optimizes the vision encoder and text encoder to extract semantic spatial features from image-text pairs via the contrastive objective.
Main Flamingo training uses a text generation (next-token prediction) objective, with the frozen LM conditioned on visual tokens via cross-attention to incorporate visual information for the next-token prediction task.
In the main phase the vision encoder is left frozen (chosen over training it directly from the text generation objective) and the pretrained LM is frozen; only the newly initialised cross-attention layers and Perceiver Resampler are trained.
